question: Your support agent handles refund requests. Policy requires two lookups in a fixed order before any decision: first get_customer, then lookup_order. After both lookups, the agent may call process_refund, call escalate_to_human, or reply to the customer in text. Which tool_choice design best enforces this order across the requests of the agentic loop?

options.text: Force get_customer on the first request, then set tool_choice to "auto" and state in the lookup_order description that it must be called next.
options.reason: With "auto", the model may call any tool or reply in text. A tool description guides the choice but does not guarantee it, so lookup_order is not ensured as the second step.

options.text: Force get_customer on the first request, force lookup_order on the next request, then set tool_choice to "auto" for the later turns.
options.reason: Forced tool selection guarantees that a specific tool is called. Forcing each required tool in turn fixes the order, and "auto" on the later turns lets the agent choose among a refund, an escalation or a text reply.

options.text: Set tool_choice to "any" on the first two requests, so that the model must call a tool before it decides or replies to the customer.
options.reason: "any" only guarantees that some tool is called. The model still chooses which tool, so it could call process_refund before the two lookups.

options.text: Force get_customer on every request until lookup_order has been called, then set tool_choice to "auto" for the later turns.
options.reason: While get_customer is forced, the model can only call get_customer, so lookup_order is never called and the condition to switch is never met. The forcing should apply to the first request only, with the next steps handled in follow-up turns.
